A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Speedy-Splat and contain the complete 14-page paper, including Appendices A.1–A.5. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original rendering-speed, image-quality, compression, and training-time results across 13 scenes, together with pruning and renderer ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, with revised scene-specific FPS entries in Table 12.

M1.justification: SnugBox, AccuTile, the efficient pruning score, and the Soft and Hard Pruning procedures are unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and their pruning schedules.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine Mip-NeRF 360, two Tanks & Temples, and two Deep Blending scenes. Table 12 changes values assigned to existing scenes, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 3–8, including the pruning-method comparisons, PUP score comparison, and StopThePop Tile-Based Culling ablation.

E3.justification: The stated preprocessing, metrics, timing procedures, pruning settings, and experimental controls are identical. Neither PDF documents a protocol revision or rerun associated with Table 12.

E4.justification: Table 12 revises the scene-specific evidence for the cumulative contributions of SnugBox, AccuTile, and pruning by reassigning FPS and speed-up entries. The component sequence, pruning-rate sweep, pruning-score comparison, and StopThePop ablations otherwise remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-run averaging practices and repeated rendering measurements in Section 5.2, Figure 7, and Tables 1 and 7. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 12 reassigns existing FPS and associated speed-ups across ten scene columns throughout the cumulative-method rows. For +Hard Pruning, truck changes from 1392 FPS (6.95×) to 1149 (6.21×), and drjohnson from 957 (6.93×) to 1122 (8.91×). The row-wise numerical sets and aggregate results remain unchanged; this is a reporting revision, not evidence of improved measured performance.

T1.justification: Equations 1–21, the Gaussian-extent and pruning-score derivations, and the AccuTile correctness sketch in Appendix A.1 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including 6.71× average rendering acceleration and 10.6× model-size reduction.

C2.justification: The explanations of rendering efficiency and pruning behavior, the speed–quality interpretation, and Section 6's limitations are unchanged. No interpretation of the Table 12 reassignment is added.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, pruning hyperparameters, CUDA-event timing, Nvidia RTX A5000 hardware, data-processing information, and the project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and related-work discussion remain, including the positioning relative to PUP 3D-GS, StopThePop, and FlashGS.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 24 March 2025 to v3 dated 14 August 2025. The prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendix structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures, table structures, captions, and page layout otherwise remain unchanged; Table 12's substantive differences are numerical.

improvement.justification: Table 12's revised truck, drjohnson, and playroom FPS entries now agree, after rounding, with the unchanged values in Figures 1 and 3. This resolves specific internal reporting inconsistencies and provides a limited quality improvement. The scientific contribution, aggregate findings, and remaining evidence are unchanged.
